key_findings: Only k=0 produced any TTFT wins: 5 of 15 head/body settings; every k>0 setting was slower than dense.
The best point was k=0, body=128, head=0 at 1.041x; this is raw copy plus RoPE, not repaired EPIC.
For k>0, the best point was k=32, body=512, head=0 at 0.829x; genuine leading-k repair never crossed dense.
Increasing exact head from 0 to 128 tokens added 8-22 ms to k>0 EPIC depending on body size because repaired tokens attend over a longer exact prefix.
Larger reusable bodies amortized fixed layerwise dispatch better, but not enough to overcome Python per-layer recompute and copy overhead on SM75.
known_limitations: This production subset supports only torch-native attention with TP=PP=DP=1 and rejects sliding-window KV pools, LoRA, MRoPE, multimodal inputs, and embedding overrides.
No semantic accuracy or output-equivalence metric was collected.

The raw matrix files were generated by the first runner revision whose metric delta window included the warmup request; TTFT rows, p50 values, cached-token checks, and zero-fallback checks are unaffected. The committed runner fixes the metric window, and this compact result reports formal-request telemetry separately.
Results are for a single 0.6B model on SM75 and do not establish behavior on RTX PRO 6000 or H100.

scope.recovery: EPIC in-request layerwise leading-k recompute plus per-layer raw body copy
